page_title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate

summary.name: Multiagent Debate (LLM Debate)
summary.one_liner: A research project showing that multiple instances of a language model proposing answers, critiquing each other, and debating over rounds improves reasoning and factual accuracy.
use_cases: improving math reasoning in language models
strategic reasoning with language model agents
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a method where several instances of the same language model propose answers, critique one another's answers, and debate over multiple rounds before giving a final answer. The default setup uses three agents debating for two rounds, and the authors note that more agents or rounds can improve results further. The authors report gains on mathematical and strategic reasoning and on factual accuracy, with fewer fallacies and hallucinations. The method works on black-box models and uses the same procedure and prompts across all tasks. The page also shows that the same procedure can combine different models, such as ChatGPT and Bard, on a grade-school math problem.
notable: Multiple instances of one LLM debate and critique each other over several rounds
Works on black-box models with the same prompts across all tasks
Can combine different models such as ChatGPT and Bard
Based on arXiv paper 2305.14325 by Du, Li, Torralba, Tenenbaum, and Mordatch
caveats: Default setup (three agents, two rounds) was chosen mainly for computational reasons
Page does not describe a downloadable tool or code; pricing and platforms are not stated
